sentences.text: Staphylococcus hominis is a bacterium frequently isolated from human skin.
It makes six distinct autoinducing peptide signals that inhibit the accessory gene regulator quorum sensing system of Staphylococcus aureus and of Staphylococcus epidermidis.
Surveys of healthy human skin found the agr-I and agr-II types of this species highly represented across subjects.
One strain produces hominicin, a heat-stable antimicrobial peptide active against Staphylococcus aureus, including methicillin-resistant and vancomycin-intermediate isolates.

Studies have reported methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus hominis as a pathogen in immunocompromised patients, and one report describes a subspecies as a nosocomial pathogen in neonates, with thirteen late-onset sepsis cases.
